input.command: cd /testbed/packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src; ls; cat preprocessor.ts 2>/dev/null; git -C /testbed diff
cd /testbed/packages/docusaurus-utils/src; grep -n "export function unwrapMdxCodeBlocks" -A40 markdownUtils.ts; grep -n "export function admonitionTitleToDirectiveLabel" -A30 markdownUtils.ts

cd /testbed/packages/docusaurus-utils/src; python3 - <<'E'
p='markdownUtils.ts'
s=open(p).read()
for n in ['```','````']:
    old=f"/(?<begin>^|\\n){n}(?<spaces>\\x20*)mdx-code-block\\n(?<children>.*?)\\n{n}(?<end>\\n|$)/gs"
    new=f"/(?<begin>^|\\r?\\n){n}(?<spaces>\\x20*)mdx-code-block\\r?\\n(?<children>.*?)\\r?\\n{n}(?<end>\\r?\\n|$)/gs"
    assert old in s; s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
sed -n 70,76p markdownUtils.ts
cat > /tmp/t.test.ts <<'E'
import {unwrapMdxCodeBlocks} from '/testbed/packages/docusaurus-utils/src/markdownUtils';
test('x',()=>{expect(unwrapMdxCodeBlocks("a\r\n```mdx-code-block\r\nimport X from 'x';\r\n```\r\nb")).toBe("a\r\nimport X from 'x';\r\nb");});
E
cp /tmp/t.test.ts __tests__/tmpcrlf.test.ts; cd /testbed; yarn jest packages/docusaurus-utils/src/__tests__/tmpcrlf.test.ts packages/docusaurus-utils/src/__tests__/markdownUtils.test.ts 2>&1 | tail -8; rm packages/docusaurus-utils/src/__tests__/tmpcrlf.test.ts

content.text:
I fixed the CRLF problem in `unwrapMdxCodeBlocks` (`packages/docusaurus-utils/src/markdownUtils.ts`). The existing `markdownUtils` tests pass, and so does a temporary CRLF test I wrote and then deleted. I didn't build a site with the issue's repro, so the full TabItem error hasn't been re-checked end to end.

**Assumed cause:** the issue's screenshot didn't come through, so I'm assuming the page wraps its `Tabs`/`TabItem` imports in a ```` ```mdx-code-block ```` fence, which is the usual pattern for this. That fence is removed by a regex that only recognised `\n` line endings. With CRLF files the regex never matched, so the import stayed inside a code block. MDX then never saw it, which produces the "Expected component `TabItem` to be defined" error. If the reporter's page doesn't use that fence, this change won't fix their case.

**Fix:** both regexes (for 3- and 4-backtick fences) now accept `\r?\n` wherever they expected `\n`. The CRLF line endings are kept in the output.

I also looked at the other preprocessing step for old-style admonition titles. It already handles CRLF, so I left it unchanged.
